subject: Hybrid introducer + resale credit framework for Obsidian Tools partnership
messages:
From: Sofia Patel <sofia@obsidian.tools>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: partnerships@obsidian.tools
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + resale credit proposal — Obsidian x Redwood

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Obsidian (we build the MQ layer for tooling integrations) is interested in a joint GTM where we both introduce leads and Obsidian can also resell a managed integration package for midsize customers.

High-level asks from our side:
- Introducer/referral credit: if Obsidian introduces a qualified opportunity that converts within 120 days, we ask for a 10% first-year revenue referral credit (paid to Obsidian on invoiced net).
- Resale margin: for customers we onboard and bill as the integrator, we need a 20% margin on Redwood monthly fees (net of discounts).
- Lead protection / double-credit: if both parties worked the same account, we want a clear attribution window and a single-credit rule (we propose first-to-file wins, with evidence).

I've attached a short business case and a zipped sample of lead intake forms to show our intake flow. Are you able to share Redwood's standard lead-registration proof requirements and any clawback windows you enforce?

Open to a short call this week to iron details.

Best,
Sofia Patel
Head of Partnerships | Obsidian Tools
sofia@obsidian.tools

Attachments: Obsidian_MQ-Partner_Business_Case.pdf (application/pdf), lead-evidence.zip (application/zip)

From: alex.martinez@redwood.com
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@obsidian.tools>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + resale credit proposal — Obsidian x Redwood

Sofia — thanks for the note and the materials. Appreciate the clarity. A few quick points from our side so we have a starting framework before a call: 

1) Intro/referral credit
- We typically do a 90-day registration window for qualified leads; 120 days is reasonable if we can align on the definition of "qualified" (MQL vs SQL).
- Standard referral credit at Redwood is 8% first-year revenue for pure introductions. We can consider 10% for strategic productized integrations if Obsidian leads the onboarding and support.

2) Resale margin
- For resold billing where Obsidian is the invoicing party, Redwood supports a margin up to 18% for partner-managed deployments. 20% is slightly above our usual cap but not a hard no — we need to map expected ARR density and support overhead.

3) Double-credit and attribution
- We enforce a single-credit rule. Our usual evidence requirement is: signed SOW/PO or last-touch email thread + HubSpot registration timestamp. First-to-file in HubSpot wins; we also accept a partner-submitted intake PDF with a timestamped contact form (your lead-evidence.zip looks useful).
- Clawback window: 12 months for deals where material misattribution is discovered, prorated on revenue.

4) Operational playbook items we need
- Lead registration form + required evidence fields (company, contact, date, qualifying notes)
- Escrow of lead artifacts (we can accept Drive link + partner attachment)
- Commission payout schedule (net 30 after invoicing)

I've looped in Ben (sales ops) and Jonas (partner GTM) to help draft a concrete matrix. Would you be available Wed 10–11am PT or Thu 2–3pm PT for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Partnerships | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia@obsidian.tools>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + resale credit proposal — Obsidian x Redwood

Quick follow-up after reviewing:

Jonas / Alex — a few redlines we should discuss with Obsidian on the call: 
- Financials: If we move to a 10% referral and 20% resale margin, we want a milestone clause tying higher credits to volume (example: >$250k ARR in 12 months unlocks the 10%/20% bands; otherwise revert to 8%/18%).
- Evidence: HubSpot registration + partner-signed intake PDF is enough for registration. For clawbacks we need contract-level documentation (signed order/SOW).
- Attribution overrides: suggest a 14-day 'good-faith' reconciliation window after registration where either party can surface competing evidence before registration is locked. This prevents stale info races.
- Reporting: require monthly partner reports (CSV export of registered leads + status) and a quarterly reconciliation.

Sofia — attaching a one-page proposed matrix (I can share a Drive link on the call). Ben signature below.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Sofia Patel <sofia@obsidian.tools>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: partnerships@obsidian.tools
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + resale credit proposal — Obsidian x Redwood

Alex / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. Wed 10am PT works for us; putting it on the calendar.

A few confirmations so the meeting can be focused: 
- We can accept an 18% resale margin if there's a volume milestone (we like your >$250k ARR unlock idea).
- We can align on a 90-day registration default and accept a 14-day reconciliation window.
- For evidence, we'll standardize the intake PDF with a Partner Signature field and timestamp (we'll include that in the attachment for the call).
- Clawbacks: 12-month prorated clawback is acceptable; we'll ask that Redwood provides a monthly visible payouts ledger for transparency.

I'll bring our commercial lead and legal counsel to the call.

See you Wed 10am PT — sending calendar invite now.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Partnerships | Obsidian Tools
